newsitem.title: USA: Banker files suit vs California lender - complaint.
newsitem.headline: Banker files suit vs California lender - complaint.

text.p: New York-based Fahnestock & Co Inc has filed suit against SeaWest Financial Corp, a Paramount, Calif.-based consumer loan originator, according to a complaint recently filed in federal court here.
Fahnestock structures asset-backed securities through its Structured Asset Sales Group.

The complaint, filed last month in Manhattan federal court, alleged that SeaWest had breached an agreement, or so-called engagement letter, with Fahnestock. The engagement letter called for Fahnestock to act as SeaWest's exclusive agent and advisor in the structuring of an asset-backed transaction, which pooled consumer loans originated by SeaWest, according to the complaint.
SeaWest denied the allegations presented in the suit and plans to respond to Fahnestock's suit soon.

"My client denies the allegation in the complaint and intends to oppose the allegation vigorously. My client does not and never has had a relationship with Fahnestock," said John Giovannone, counsel for SeaWest at Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton, a Los Angeles-based law firm.
The complaint said the engagement letter called for Fahnestock to act as SeaWest's agent in securing a commitment for subordinated debt and in securing a warehouse loan.
The engagement letter was agreed to by SeaWest and Gruntal Structured Asset Sales Group on May 3, 1996, according to the complaint.
Gruntal's Structured Asset Sales Group, a unit of Gruntal & Co and headed by David Pullman, picked up and moved over to Fahnestock earlier this year.
According to the complaint, Fahnestock acquired all rights and obligations of Gruntal & Co Inc in connection with the engagement letter agreed to by Gruntal and Seawest.

In its suit, Fahnestock alleged that SeaWest broke tenets agreed to in the engagement letter when it agreed to sell its subordinated debt to Levine Leichtman Capital Partners Inc of Beverly Hills, Calif. According to the complaint, the contract with Levine Leichtman became effective "in or about March 1997."

Also, Fahnestock alleged that the Paramount, Calif.-based lender broke tenets agreed upon in the engagement letter when Seawest hired Finova Capital Corp in which Finova allegedly agreed to provide a warehouse loan in the amount of $25 million. The agreement with Finova, according to the complaint, was made "in or about March 1997."

The complaint indicated that Fahnestock had solicited on SeaWest's behalf a warehouse loan facility with ING Capital in the amount of $50 million. "The ING Capital transaction was not consummated because SeaWest failed to provide certain information in the format reasonably required by ING Capital," Fahnestock alleged in the complaint.

Breach of the engagement letter, according to the document, has Fahnestock seeking over $3.0 million in damages, plus interest, "including Fahnestock's fees for the additional financial transactions that defendant projected to occur during the remainder of the engagement period."
